claude_take: What strikes me across today's stories is how unglamorous AI's real advance looks up close: it's showing up in Black Friday checkout flows and Instagram inboxes, and even David Fincher describes it as a way to shave takes off a shoot rather than replace actors. Meanwhile the stories about raw institutional weight point the other way: a federal judge checking the FCC's retaliation against a broadcaster, and Louis Vuitton bumping against the limits of its own growth machine, both show that scale eventually runs into friction, whether that friction is a constitution or just consumer fatigue. AI is becoming infrastructure precisely by not looking like a revolution anymore, which is exactly when it is worth paying the most attention to it.
claude_take_title: AI Is Becoming Infrastructure by Not Looking Like One

items.headline: David Fincher Explains How He Used AI in Post-Production on 'Cliff Booth'
items.summary: Director David Fincher said in a new interview that he used AI tools during post-production on his upcoming film built around the Cliff Booth character, to reduce the number of takes needed while keeping performances rooted in real actors. Fincher framed the technology as a production aid rather than a replacement for human performers, a notable data point as major directors begin discussing AI workflows candidly rather than denying their use.

items.headline: Walmart Partners With Meta's Muse AI Agent for Black Friday Shopping
items.summary: Walmart is letting shoppers complete Black Friday purchases through Meta's Muse AI agent, with users able to set spending limits and approve each purchase before it goes through. The deal signals growing retailer comfort with agentic AI handling real transactions during the industry's highest-stakes shopping window, and contrasts with Amazon, which has reportedly kept Muse blocked from its own marketplace.

items.headline: Netflix Closes Its Roughly $400 Million Purchase of Radford Studio Center
items.summary: Netflix has completed its purchase of the historic Radford Studio Center in Studio City, ending a monthslong saga that included a foreclosure sale after the lot's previous operator defaulted on its mortgage. The streamer called the deal a "meaningful new investment" in California's film industry, giving it a major new production hub as it expands its physical production footprint.

items.headline: Oscars Visual Effects Branch Narrows Field to 20, Disney Leads With Four Films
items.summary: The Academy's Visual Effects Branch has confirmed its shortlist of 20 films in contention for the Best Visual Effects Oscar, with Disney placing four titles including Dune: Part Three and The Odyssey. The list is an early signal of which effects-driven blockbusters the industry sees as top contenders heading into formal nominations, and a marker of how concentrated the year's biggest VFX work remains at a handful of major studios.

items.headline: Meta Brings Its Muse AI Agent Directly Into Instagram DMs
items.summary: Meta has added its Muse personal AI agent to Instagram's direct messages, starting in the US, Canada, Mexico, Japan and Singapore, letting users chat with an AI assistant inside the same inbox they use for friends. The move pushes a general-purpose AI agent deeper into one of the world's largest social apps, continuing a broader shift of AI assistants from standalone chat apps into the feeds and inboxes people already use daily.

items.headline: Federal Judge Rules FCC's Review of ABC's Licenses Violated the First Amendment
items.summary: A federal judge issued a preliminary injunction finding that the FCC's early review of ABC's broadcast licenses amounted to unlawful retaliation against the network's speech, citing public statements by President Trump and FCC Chair Brendan Carr attacking ABC and Disney. The ruling blocks the license reviews for now, though the underlying case continues, and Disney/ABC called it "an important victory for the First Amendment."

items.headline: Is LVMH's Louis Vuitton Past Its Peak?
items.summary: Business of Fashion reports that LVMH is struggling to chart a new growth phase for Louis Vuitton, its largest and most profitable brand, after years of blistering expansion gave way to softer demand, shifting tastes and a leadership transition as Pietro Beccari now also runs the wider LVMH Fashion Group. Because Vuitton has long been the engine powering LVMH's profits, its stall matters for the whole conglomerate, not just one house.

items.headline: Descartes's Cogito, Ergo Sum
items.headline_fr: Le cogito de Descartes : « Je pense, donc je suis »
items.summary: In his Meditations, René Descartes tried to strip away every belief that could possibly be doubted, including the evidence of his senses and even the existence of the physical world, to find one claim immune to doubt. He found it in the act of doubting itself: the fact that he is thinking proves that he exists, since there must be a thinker for the thought to belong to. The cogito matters today because it models a method, not just a conclusion: when you cannot trust an institution, a source, or your own perceptions, you can still start from what survives radical doubt and rebuild outward from there.
items.summary_fr: Dans ses Méditations, René Descartes s'efforce d'écarter toute croyance qui pourrait être mise en doute, y compris le témoignage des sens et jusqu'à l'existence du monde physique, afin de trouver une certitude à l'épreuve du doute. Il la trouve dans l'acte même de douter : le fait de penser prouve qu'il existe, puisqu'une pensée suppose nécessairement quelqu'un qui pense. Le cogito garde toute sa pertinence aujourd'hui car il propose une méthode, pas seulement une conclusion : lorsqu'on ne peut plus se fier à une institution, à une source ou même à ses propres perceptions, il reste possible de repartir de ce qui résiste au doute radical pour reconstruire son savoir pas à pas.
